title: "Step3.effect-size-correlation-bulk-vs-single-cell"

Testing: all sc2glu-tested SNPs vs. bulk's significant calls (does bulk's significant signal for a gene hold up, directionally and quantitatively, when re-examined in sc2glu, whether or not sc2glu itself calls it significant)

"of all eQTLs tested in sc2glu per phenotype, how many are found in bulk's significant eQTL list and do they show effect size and sign concordance"

library(tidyverse)

```{r}
save_my_plot <- function(plot, name, width = 5, height = 5, out_dir = "../results") {
  dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in")
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".png")), plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 300)
  invisible(NULL)
}
```


```{r}
library(tidyverse)

PATHS_sc2glu <- list(
  SNPs = "/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all/sc2glu.2/fastlmm/results/results_SNPs_968_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run2/"
)

# ============================================================
# STEP 1 — genes tested in sc2glu = gene subfolders under SNPs dir
# ============================================================
sc2glu_tested_genes <- list.dirs(PATHS_sc2glu$SNPs, recursive = FALSE, full.names = FALSE)
cat("Genes with a sc2glu SNP association file:", length(sc2glu_tested_genes), "\n")

# ============================================================
# STEP 2 — reader for one gene's full (all-SNPs-tested) file
# ============================================================
read_sc2glu_gene_tests <- function(gene, snps_dir) {
  f <- file.path(snps_dir, gene, paste0(gene, ".first_assoc.txt"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  tryCatch({
    read.table(f, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "") %>%
      transmute(SNP, Beta_sc = SnpWeight, P_sc = PValue, Gene = gene)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}

# ============================================================
# STEP 3 — bulk (Caudal / pan-transcriptome) side
# SNP ids already match sc2glu's own SNP column format
# ("rs_chromosomeN_pos"), and the effect-size column in both
# datasets is SnpWeight — no reformatting or renaming needed.
# ============================================================
bulk_snps <- snp_pan_transcriptome %>%
  transmute(SNP, Beta_bulk = SnpWeight, P_bulk = PValue, Gene = Pheno)

# ============================================================
# STEP 4 — retrieve + join, gene by gene
# NOTE ON SCALE: reads one file per gene (potentially thousands).
# Test on a subset first:  sc2glu_tested_genes <- head(sc2glu_tested_genes, 25)
# ============================================================
all_tested_concordance <- map_dfr(seq_along(sc2glu_tested_genes), function(i) {
  gene <- sc2glu_tested_genes[i]
  if (i %% 200 == 0) cat(sprintf("  [%d/%d genes]\n", i, length(sc2glu_tested_genes)))

  sc_gene <- read_sc2glu_gene_tests(gene, PATHS_sc2glu$SNPs)
  if (is.null(sc_gene) || nrow(sc_gene) == 0) return(NULL)

  bulk_gene <- bulk_snps %>% filter(Gene == gene)
  if (nrow(bulk_gene) == 0) return(NULL)

  inner_join(sc_gene, bulk_gene %>% select(SNP, Beta_bulk, P_bulk), by = "SNP")
})

cat("\nTotal matched SNP x gene pairs (sc2glu tested, found in bulk):",
    nrow(all_tested_concordance), "\n")
cat("Genes contributing at least one matched SNP:",
    n_distinct(all_tested_concordance$Gene), "\n")


# ============================================================
# STEP 5 — effect size concordance statistics (generic, reusable)
# ============================================================
calculate_effect_size_concordance <- function(df, beta1_col, beta2_col,
                                               cond1_name, cond2_name,
                                               n_perms = 5000) {
  beta1 <- df[[beta1_col]]
  beta2 <- df[[beta2_col]]
  n     <- length(beta1)

  same_sign <- sign(beta1) == sign(beta2)
  n_concord <- sum(same_sign, na.rm = TRUE)
  sign_conc <- n_concord / n

  obs_r   <- cor(beta1, beta2, method = "pearson",  use = "complete.obs")
  obs_rho <- cor(beta1, beta2, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")

  binom_res <- binom.test(n_concord, n, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater")

  perm_sign <- replicate(n_perms, {
    perm_beta2 <- sample(beta2)
    sum(sign(beta1) == sign(perm_beta2), na.rm = TRUE) / n
  })
  perm_r <- replicate(n_perms, {
    perm_beta2 <- sample(beta2)
    cor(beta1, perm_beta2, method = "pearson", use = "complete.obs")
  })

  cat(sprintf("\n%s vs %s — effect size concordance (n = %d SNP x gene pairs)\n",
              cond1_name, cond2_name, n))
  cat(sprintf("  Sign concordance: %.1f%% (binomial p = %.3e)\n",
              100 * sign_conc, binom_res$p.value))
  cat(sprintf("  Pearson r:    %.4f (permutation p = %.4f)\n",
              obs_r, sum(perm_r >= obs_r) / n_perms))
  cat(sprintf("  Spearman rho: %.4f\n", obs_rho))

  list(data = df, n = n, n_concordant = n_concord, sign_conc = sign_conc,
       obs_r = obs_r, obs_rho = obs_rho, binom_result = binom_res,
       perm_sign = perm_sign, perm_r = perm_r,
       perm_p_sign = sum(perm_sign >= sign_conc) / n_perms,
       perm_p_r = sum(perm_r >= obs_r) / n_perms)
}

sc_bulk_stats <- calculate_effect_size_concordance(
  all_tested_concordance, "Beta_sc", "Beta_bulk",
  cond1_name = "sc2glu (all tested)", cond2_name = "Bulk (Caudal 2024)"
)

# ============================================================
# STEP 6 — plots (uses save_plot() already defined in this file)
# ============================================================
fig_effect_scatter <- ggplot(sc_bulk_stats$data, aes(x = Beta_sc, y = Beta_bulk)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = sign(Beta_sc) == sign(Beta_bulk)), alpha = 0.3, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#27AE60", `FALSE` = "#E74C3C"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "Concordant", `FALSE` = "Discordant"),
                      name = "Direction") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.3,
           label = sprintf("Pearson r = %.3f\nSpearman rho = %.3f\nSign concordance = %.1f%%\nn = %d",
                            sc_bulk_stats$obs_r, sc_bulk_stats$obs_rho,
                            100 * sc_bulk_stats$sign_conc, sc_bulk_stats$n),
           size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = "Effect size concordance: sc2glu (all tested) vs. Bulk (Caudal 2024)",
       x = "Effect size beta, sc2glu", y = "Effect size beta, bulk") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "right")

save_my_plot(fig_effect_scatter, "SC2GLU_vs_Bulk_effect_size_concordance", width = 6.5, height = 5.5)

perm_df <- data.frame(sign_conc = sc_bulk_stats$perm_sign, pearson_r = sc_bulk_stats$perm_r)

fig_null_sign <- ggplot(perm_df, aes(x = sign_conc)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey70", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sc_bulk_stats$sign_conc, color = "#E74C3C", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Sign concordance — permutation null", x = "Sign concordance", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

fig_null_r <- ggplot(perm_df, aes(x = pearson_r)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey70", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sc_bulk_stats$obs_r, color = "#27AE60", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Pearson r — permutation null", x = "Pearson r", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

save_my_plot(fig_null_sign, "SC2GLU_vs_Bulk_null_sign_concordance", width = 5, height = 4)
save_my_plot(fig_null_r,    "SC2GLU_vs_Bulk_null_pearson_r",        width = 5, height = 4)
```
